_comment: Rendered by web/index.html. Edit this, not the HTML. Keep 'blocked' honest — a page that is all green is a page nobody believes.

milestones.name: Corpus measures
milestones.note: Caption coverage, anchor coverage, sibling ambiguity and page sharing, computed on two extraction pipelines that share no code and no models. Model-free, so it reproduces anywhere.

milestones.name: Placement metric
milestones.note: Ground truth derived from the source typesetting rather than annotation. Retriever and generator both removed, so what is measured is the placement mechanism alone.

milestones.name: External validation
milestones.note: MRAMG-Bench Academic subset, n=200, gold authored by that benchmark's authors. Configuration frozen before the dataset was downloaded. Leads the published comparators, and still leads when forced to emit an image on every question.

milestones.name: Selection result
milestones.note: The composed selector reaches F1 0.605 against human annotation — but on 48 items carrying 19 positive links. This is the number a reviewer will push hardest on, and the sample is the binding constraint on it.

milestones.name: Annotation scale-up
milestones.note: Target is roughly 200 items plus a second annotator, and that part is still human work. But the judge that would carry a scale-up now has a measured agreement of kappa 0.662 on the protocol it would scale, and a rectified estimator is implemented. It refuses its own data today: the doubly-labelled pairs are 2.46x enriched in positives. The remaining blocker is compute, not annotation.

milestones.name: Bibliography
milestones.note: Every entry checked against its arXiv or publisher listing page. No entry remains marked unverified.

milestones.name: Authorship and venue
milestones.note: The author list is deliberately unfilled in main.tex and CITATION.cff. Venue is undecided: the running header currently reads as a preprint, and the title was rewritten to name the method rather than the deployment.

milestones.name: Judge-scaled estimation
milestones.note: A prediction-powered estimator that lets judge labels stand in for annotation without inheriting the judge's bias — if the judge is useless it degrades to human-only rather than going wrong. Implemented, gated, and currently refusing to report on its own data.

notes: The method is a join over data the layout parser already produced. No model, no training, nothing tuned per corpus — so the claim is not scoped to a language or a document genre.
The Indonesian textbook corpus is the stress case, not the scope: only a fifth of its figures carry a printed caption, so a caption-matching pipeline fails there in a way caption-rich corpora hide.
